text: List comprehensions are one of Python's most loved features — they build a whole list in a single readable line.
The pattern is: the expression you want, then for, then the item, then the sequence.
So x times two for x in numbers doubles every value, replacing a three-line loop entirely.
[chuckle] Add an if at the end and it becomes a filter — keep only the numbers where the condition is true.
Here we keep just the even ones, all in that same compact line.
[sniff] And you can do both at once — transform and filter together, squaring only the even numbers.
Comprehensions work on any sequence, not just numbers — here we uppercase every word in a list.
[groan] You can even nest them to build a grid, a list of lists, with one comprehension inside another.
Just don't overdo the nesting — if it stops being readable, a plain loop is the kinder choice.
Video 21 tackles dict comprehensions. Follow so you don't miss it.
